messages:
Alex Chen: Quick RFC follow-up. After the private control-plane split spike, I prototyped a tiny tenant-side agent to handle egress handoff for ephemeral workloads (think: ephemeral pods that need stable source IP + low-latency control plane calls). Wanted to call out tradeoffs before we commit to a pattern.

Alex Chen: Goals: preserve client source IP for tenant egress when possible, avoid expensive cross-account NAT for every flow, and keep TLS end-to-end (no termination in our CP).

Maria Lopez: Nice. What are the failure modes here? e.g., agent crash, lost certs, DNS skew between agent and control plane?

Alex Chen: Good questions. Failure modes I saw: 1) Agent loses cert -> control plane rejects -> workload falls back to public endpoint (we should automate). 2) Stale DNS in the tenant -> connection attempts to old relay IPs. 3) When we try to preserve source IP via hairpinned proxy we can accidentally cause asymmetric routing for other infra.

Sam Kim: Can you sketch the proposed behavior and config? short pseudo-config is fine.

Alex Chen: Sure:
```yaml
agent:
  mode: tcp-proxy # passthrough TLS
  preserve_source_ip: true
  mtls_identity: rotated-client-cert
  fallback: public-relay, exponential-backoff
  controlplane_endpoint: cp-internal.example:8443
  metrics_endpoint: 127.0.0.1:9000
```
(Agent keeps a local connection pool to the tenant-vpc relay, reuses TLS sessions so we don't pay handshake penalty per request)

Jordan V: For preserving IPs are we assuming the agent runs with hostNetwork or uses iptables TPROXY? hostNetwork has security implications; TPROXY needs kernel tweaks and CNI support. Which direction?

Alex Chen: Prototype used hostNetwork inside a DaemonSet (faster to iterate), but that won't fly for tenants that reject host network. Long-term I propose two modes: 1) hostNetwork/daemon for Dedicated/Trusted tenants; 2) sidecar TPROXY mode for general tenants (CNI opt-in).

Maria Lopez: How do we handle certs/key management? We can't put long-lived keys in tenants. Need short-lived certs minted by CP KMS with automated rotation. Also we must be able to revoke quickly if agent compromised.

Sam Kim: Agreed. Plan: CP issues short-lived mTLS client certs (15m default) via the customer control channel; agent auto-refreshes using a local-to-controlplane bootstrap token stored in the tenant secret store (KMS-protected). Revocation via server-side blacklist + short lifetime.

Alex Chen: Also must preserve observability: traces/req ids must flow across the agent boundary. Suggest we inject an edge header on the internal path (not user-visible) and emit the same into CP logs so traces correlate.

Jordan V: What's the fallback UX? If agent can't preserve IP or fails, do we silently fail over to hosted relay? That could change egress billing and source IP expectations for customers. We need explicit customer notification and a configurable fallback policy.

Alex Chen: I think default fallback: 1) try local agent path for X seconds; 2) if failing, fall back to hosted relay but mark flows with "fallback.reason=agent-unavailable" in logs and emit a customer-facing event in the Console. Fallback policy must be configurable per-tenant.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for agent v0.3 -> region us-west-2 -> customers: beta-tenant-3, demo-tenant-1

Maria Lopez: Ops/security ask: add an emergency kill-switch that forces all traffic via hosted endpoint (for < 5min incidents) and ability to rotate agent bootstrap tokens across all tenants quickly.

Alex Chen: Agreed. Proposed rollout plan: Phase 0 (canary) run hostNetwork daemon for two trusted tenants, collect metrics (error rate, CPU, conn churn, TLS handshakes). Phase 1 (opt-in) release sidecar TPROXY image + docs. Phase 2 (default) auto-opt-in for tenants that opt-in in Console + policy controls.

Sam Kim: Quick perf note: reuse TLS sessions between agent and relay, and expose a pooled connection count in metrics. In our tests TLS session reuse cut CPU ~3x for short-lived requests.

Ops Lead: Please produce a one-pager with: 1) security model (cert lifecycle + revocation), 2) operator playbook (kill-switch + canary rollback), 3) customer-facing fallback docs, 4) perf targets (p95 latency delta <= 5ms). Can we have that by EOD Friday?

Alex Chen: I can draft the one-pager and a simple test harness (load generator + metric dashboards) by Friday. I'll also add a short note about required CNI tweaks for TPROXY mode.

Jordan V: If we go hostNetwork for Dedicated tenants, we should add a checklist for tenant infra approval (SOC/Network review).

Maria Lopez: One more callout: DNS propagation window. If agent uses pinned relay IPs, we need a fast re-resolve and backoff strategy. Add a TTL-based jittered re-resolve and a short-circuit to fallback if DNS repeatedly fails.

Alex Chen: Noted. I'll include TTL jitter logic and circuit-breaker behavior in the implementation doc.

Alex Chen: TL;DR: implement a small tenant-side agent (tcp-proxy passthrough + optional TPROXY) with short-lived mTLS, metrics + trace propagation, configurable fallback to hosted relay, and a staged rollout with kill-switch and operator playbooks.

Maria Lopez: Sounds good. Thanks, Alex.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary metrics dashboard created -> https://dashboards.internal/redwood/agent-v0.3-canary

Ops Lead: Adding action item: Alex to share one-pager + test harness link; Sam to validate TLS session reuse perf numbers; Maria to draft operator runbook. Follow-up sync Monday 10am.
